sources.title: Concordance of Arcane Space (Spelljammer: AD&D Adventures in Space)
Astral Adventurer's Guide (Spelljammer: Adventures in Space)

summary.2e: The rainbow-colored, flammable medium that fills the space between the crystal spheres. Currents in it (the Flow) carry ships between spheres.
summary.5e: The silvery plane between the wildspace systems. A ship moves through it when its captain concentrates on a destination.

regions.name: The Known Spheres
regions.summary: A stable group of spheres around the triangle of Realmspace, Greyspace and Krynnspace, with Herospace, Greatspace, Darkspace, Faeriespace and Clusterspace. Some books use the name for the core three alone, or for all of known space.

regions.name: Arcane Inner Flow
regions.summary: A stable group of fewer than a dozen spheres near Realmspace, among them Refuge, Pirtelspace and Darnannonspace. Two-way currents join its neighbors.

regions.name: Vodoni Empire
regions.summary: Twelve spheres that Emperor Vulkaran the Dark rules from Vodonispace. Its currents reach Realmspace, Greyspace and Krynnspace.

spheres.name: Realmspace
spheres.summary: The crystal sphere around Toril's system. Glyphs hundreds of miles tall cover the inside of the shell, and the stars are openings to the quasi-elemental plane of Radiance.
facts: Glyphs and wards hundreds of miles tall line the inside. Reading one releases a spell at 100 times normal power.
About 3,200 open at any time. The Wanderers, a line of cursed souls who walk the inside of the shell, chant them open.

bodies.name: The Sun
bodies.summary: The primary of Realmspace, at the exact center of the sphere. Creatures from the elemental plane of Fire live on it, and they attack any ship that comes within ten million miles.
facts: Creatures from the elemental plane of Fire

bodies.name: The Sargassos
bodies.summary: Twelve magic-dead globes, each 100,000 miles across, on an orbit 40 million miles from the Sun. Helms and magic items stop inside them.
facts: Helms fade, then stop. The helmsman falls into spelljammer shock for four days.

bodies.name: Anadia
bodies.summary: The innermost planet, small and amber-green, cut by canyons larger than the Great Rift. Halflings live at both poles. The hot equator belongs to umber hulks and other Anadian beasts.
facts: Halflings at the poles, umber hulks at the equator
Once used as a debris storage area

bodies.name: Coliar
bodies.summary: A huge world of air. Floating islands of earth and water orbit its core, between 50 and 30,000 miles from the center. Avian humanoids and reptiles live on them.
facts: Floats about 100 miles above the core

bodies.name: Toril
bodies.summary: The third planet and the most populous world in Realmspace, with the widest variety of life. Selûne orbits it, and the Tears of Selûne trail behind the moon.
facts: Chunming in Shou Lung, and Calimport, where ships must land on the water away from the city

bodies.name: Selûne
bodies.summary: Toril's moon, 183,000 miles out. The same side always faces Toril. Its people worship Leira, and most of them are elves and humans.

bodies.name: Tears of Selûne
bodies.summary: A cluster of asteroids that trails behind Selûne on the same orbit, 183,000 miles from Toril. Elves and humans live here, with other spacefaring races.
facts: Elves and humans, with a smattering of other spacefaring races

bodies.name: Rock of Bral
bodies.summary: An asteroid in the Tears of Selûne and the site of the city of Bral, a port for spelljamming ships from many spheres.

sources.title: Faiths & Avatars (cited by the Forgotten Realms Wiki)

bodies.name: Karpri
bodies.summary: An ocean world. Pack ice hundreds of miles thick covers the poles, and mats of weed on the equator carry huge insects. Aquatic elves live in the seas.
facts: Aquatic elves, huge insects, arctic predators

bodies.name: Chandos
bodies.summary: A water world. Rocks pile up in its seas into islands that do not stay stable. The people descend from the crews of two spelljammers that crashed here long ago.

bodies.name: Glyth
bodies.summary: A harsh gray world with a ring and three moons. Mind flayers have held it for about a century, and most activity happens underground.
facts: Mind flayers and many humanoid races

bodies.name: Rings of Glyth
bodies.summary: A ring of small asteroids and ice balls around Glyth's equator. The mind flayers keep captive oortlings on it.

bodies.name: Haven
bodies.summary: A hollowed asteroid between the first and second rings of Glyth. Warring mind flayer factions treat it as neutral ground.
facts: Between Glyth's first and second rings

bodies.name: Mingabwe
bodies.summary: A bitterly cold moon of Glyth and a trading post for merchants who are not mind flayers.

bodies.name: Polluter
bodies.summary: A small, unmapped moon that orbits Mingabwe.

bodies.name: Garden
bodies.summary: Not one world but a chain of earth masses held together by one enormous plant, Yggdrasil's Child. It has twelve moons, and pirates have dens here.

bodies.name: H'Catha
bodies.summary: A flat disc of water 300 miles thick with one mountain, the Spindle, at its center. The Spindle always points at the Sun. Beholders hold the world.

bodies.name: Turnbetl
bodies.summary: The closer moon of H'Catha. Its atmosphere is made of highly unstable gases.

bodies.name: Lumbe
bodies.summary: The farthest moon of H'Catha: a metal cylinder 600 by 75 feet that tumbles like a baton. Behind two locked doors is an empty mage's laboratory.

bodies.name: Comet K'Thoutek
bodies.summary: A comet of iron and ice about 300 miles across. It travels at right angles to the planets' orbits and takes more than 237 years to go around the Sun. Toril's astrologers read great births in its appearances.
facts: Only within 200 million miles of the Sun

bodies.name: Skull of the Void
bodies.summary: A human skull of bone 12 miles high and 10 miles wide. It does not move and orbits nothing, about 50 million miles inside the shell. It repairs itself and makes its own air.
facts: Fixed, about 50 million miles from the shell

bodies.name: Caer Windlauer
bodies.summary: A castle with ten spires on 2,000 acres of land, sent into orbit around the Sun by a wish. Its orbit runs between Coliar's and Karpri's distances, at 45 degrees to Toril's.
facts: 100 to 300 million miles from the Sun, tilted 45 degrees
About 2,000 acres, with a pond and streams that flow in a circle

bodies.name: Galleon Nebula
bodies.summary: A nebula shaped like a multicolored galleon under sail, two million miles long and high. Through a spyglass its oars seem to row. Toril sees it mostly in autumn and early winter.
facts: 2 million miles long and high, over 100,000 miles wide

bodies.name: Color Spray Nebula
bodies.summary: A fan-shaped nebula that looks like a color spray spell, about two million miles long. Worshipers of Mystra take it as a sign of her favor. Toril sees it in spring and early summer.
facts: About 2 million miles long, 1 million wide at the open end

spheres.name: Greyspace
spheres.summary: The crystal sphere of the world Oerth, one of the largest known. Oerth is the primary at the center, and the sun Liga orbits it. The shell is 16,000 million miles across.
facts: 16,000 million miles. The radius is 8,000 million miles, which is two times the orbit of the Spectre.
Oerth, at the center. Liga, the sun, orbits Oerth.
Kule, Raenei, Liga, the Grinder, Edill, Gnibile, Conatha, Ginsel, Borka, Greela and the Spectre orbit Oerth, from nearest to farthest.
The Great Sargasso, the Dark Stars, the Habitat and the Sisters orbit between the Spectre and the shell.
At top spelljamming speed: 40 days from Oerth to the Spectre, 80 days to the shell, 160 days across the sphere.
The outer face is mirror-bright with a pearl sheen. The inner face is black and absorbs all light. Nothing can scratch, dent or melt the shell.
The stars are bright jewels set in the shell. The largest are 10 to 20 miles across, and most are less than 1 mile. At 100 feet or less from one, the heat is thousands of degrees.
Less than 24 portals are open at one time. Most are tens of feet wide. At intervals of about 5 years, a portal some miles wide opens.
In an 11-year cycle, 10 times as many portals are open for 2 months. The total is always less than 250.
A constant 40 to 45 degrees Fahrenheit. It is hotter near Liga.
Most bodies orbit in one plane. Only Ginsel and the Spectre tilt away from it.

bodies.name: Oerth
bodies.summary: The world at the center of Greyspace. All other bodies in the sphere orbit it, the sun Liga too. Humans and humanoid races are the most numerous.
facts: 365 days (the orbit of Liga sets it)
The Free City of Greyhawk, Dyvers and Irongate

bodies.name: Kule
bodies.summary: The closer and smaller moon of Oerth, also called Celene. It has no air, and an unknown race left seven deserted cities on it. Drow, mind flayers and kuo-toa live underground.
facts: Spherical earth body with no air (a voidworld)
91 days (one face always points at Oerth)
Drow (about 20,000), mind flayers (about 15,000) and kuo-toa (about 5,000), all underground
Kule looks as large as Liga from Oerth, so it makes total eclipses of the sun

bodies.name: Raenei
bodies.summary: The larger moon of Oerth, also called Luna. It has air, seas and weather like Oerth, but less oxygen. No native creature has more than average intelligence.
facts: D, about half the width of Oerth
Animals, many of them monsters, with a small number of settlers and hermits
Triumph, a village of more than 200 humans near the north pole

bodies.name: Liga
bodies.summary: The sun of Greyspace, a fire world about 75,000 miles across. It orbits Oerth in 364 days. Thousands of lakes of cool elemental water dot its surface.
facts: Spherical fire body that is shorter from pole to pole
G, about 75,000 miles across. The core is 1,000 miles wide, and the layer of fire above it is 37,000 miles deep.
Fire creatures, water elementals in the lakes, and a colony of efreet in a bronze castle
29 fire bands, each 1,000 miles wide. The outer band does 1d6 damage each round, and each band nearer Liga adds 1d6.

bodies.name: The Moth
bodies.summary: A small, airless rock that orbits Liga, 15,000 miles above the photosphere. One face always points at the sun and burns. The other face is bitterly cold.
facts: 15,000 miles above the photosphere, about 52,500 miles from the center
Thousands of degrees. A creature takes 15d6 damage each round.
So cold that it does 8d6 damage each round without magical protection
About 100 yards wide, with a moderate temperature. Explorers use it as a camp to study Liga.

bodies.name: The Grinder
bodies.summary: A dense field of rocks. The largest are 100 miles wide, and the smallest are as small as golf balls. The rocks make a hollow sphere around Oerth and the inner planets, so all ships bound for Oerth must go through it.
facts: B (the largest rocks are about 100 miles across)
Members of most spacefaring races, and undead
About 100,000 rocks are class A, and at most 200 are class B. Ceres is the most important settlement. A rumored undead rock is called Reaper.

bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.summary: The largest rock of the Grinder, also called the Pup, and the site of its most important settlement. It is shaped like a kidney, with a lake 10 miles wide. About 250 residents live in the town.
facts: 10 miles wide, in the saddle of the rock. Ships can come down on the lake or on a smooth area of rock.
About 250, mostly human. A quarter are demihumans, and a dozen giff and two reigar live there.
No food crop grows here, so Ceres depends on trade. The residents elect a Harbormaster for a term of 3 years.

bodies.name: Khadazah
bodies.summary: A rock in the Grinder, also called Motherlode. Dwarf miners claim it, and their citadel ship orbits it with its weapons always crewed. The mines give zinc and copper.
facts: Zinc, copper and lead. Rumors say the dwarves also found gold, and some say mithril.
The citadel keeps its weapon platforms crewed against claim-jumpers

bodies.name: Lassh'tz Zst'q
bodies.summary: A small outpost of lizardmen on a small rock in the Grinder. The rock is warm and humid, with a surface of shallow swamps and ponds.
facts: The lizardman name means "We are here."
Swamp (Oerth humans), Cenerea (Toril elves), Harkalopenarigastinoven (Krynnish gnomes)

bodies.name: Skullbringer
bodies.summary: A rock in the Grinder with a small, new colony of mind flayers. The illithids trade with the other rock settlements.
facts: A small mind flayer colony, founded recently
Some sages think the illithids came from the world of Falx
One captain saw a neogi mindspider here. This is not confirmed.

bodies.name: Edill
bodies.summary: A large ball of air almost 100,000 miles across, with no solid core. Thousands of dragons live here, most of them silver. 20,736 bodies each of rock, fire and water orbit in the air.
facts: Dragons, with some avians and other reptiles. About 95 in 100 dragons are metallic.
Skyhaven, a rock 3 miles wide with 100 or more silver dragons. The Diver holds 75 hostile red dragons.

bodies.name: Gnibile
bodies.summary: A large ball of air 96,000 miles across, wrapped in red clouds of poison and acid that are 500 yards thick. Undead rule the rock islands in it. Storms and lightning light its dark depths.
facts: Undead, and the porton, a creature that opens gates to the negative quasi-elemental planes
A rock 2 miles wide, 10 miles below the clouds, with a city of undead. The warrior-lich Samanda rules it.

bodies.name: Conatha
bodies.summary: An oval world of salt water, 800 miles long and 600 miles wide, that turns end for end as it orbits. No island shows above the sea, and the air is clear and calm. Sahuagin and mermen fight in the depths.
facts: C, 800 miles long and 600 miles wide
Sahuagin, mermen, whales and other sea life
Loquasti and Varanais sit 100 miles apart at the two foci. A merman nation lives on each.

bodies.name: Ginsel
bodies.summary: A world shaped like a sphere with a large bite taken out. Air and gravity continue across the edge and into the bite. More than 3 million humans live in more than two dozen nations.
facts: C, about 1,000 miles from pole to pole
More than 3 million humans, with some demihumans
Tarvin in Yendoril, Gord City and Costepen

bodies.name: Borka
bodies.summary: A cluster of thousands of rocks in one shared air envelope, about 5,000 miles across. It was a world until elves shattered it in the first Unhuman War. Orcs, goblins and other humanoids live here.
facts: A for each rock, from less than 500 yards to almost 10 miles wide. The cluster is about 5,000 miles across.
240 months. The rocks orbit the center of the cluster in almost 100 years.
Orcs, goblins, hobgoblins, kobolds and other humanoids
Potemkiz, 5 miles wide at the edge, is a decoy outpost. The Egg, 10 miles by 7 miles, is a secret fleet dock.

bodies.name: Greela
bodies.summary: A cluster of hundreds of planetoids in one thin air envelope, about 9,000 miles across. Humans and elves live here. The elves make ships of living crystal in their shipyard.
facts: E, about 9,000 miles across. Each planetoid is tens to hundreds of miles wide.
Varies. The largest planetoids have days of 20 to 35 hours.
360 months. The planetoids orbit the center of the cluster in about 40 years.
Humans and elves, with some other demihumans and non-evil giants
Cenbreadiné on the elven planetoid Cenalterien, and Bonanza, the largest town of the human nation Frontier

bodies.name: The Spectre
bodies.summary: A flat disk about 100 miles wide and 10 miles thick at the edge. It spins like a tossed coin, so it seems to wink out when seen edge-on. No life arose here, but many races keep outposts.
facts: Disk earth body, also called the Wink
B, about 100 miles across and 10 miles thick at the edge
16 hours (the tumble). It also turns on its own axis in 35 days.
Traders, elves, dwarves, gnomes, mind flayers and beholders at outposts. No native life.
Three human trading posts and the elven navy post Tranmielé on the north face. The mind flayer post Skulls-in-a-Row is on the south face.

bodies.name: The Sisters
bodies.summary: Nine blue-white quasi-stars: eight in an octagon around a ninth. From Oerth they look like one bright star. A ship that crosses the plane of the stars can move in space or in time.
facts: Nine quasi-stars, each a sphere 1 mile wide
Eight stars make an octagon around the ninth. The octagon is 500 miles across and always faces Oerth.
7,500 million miles from Oerth, at right angles to the ecliptic. One orbit takes 400 months.
The eight outer stars orbit the central star in 12 months
Their light dazzles at 1 million miles or less and blinds at 250,000 miles or less. They give no heat.
A field pushes objects away from 100 miles out. No ship can get nearer than about 1 mile.
A ship that crosses the plane can go to a different position in the sphere, to a different sphere, or to a different time

bodies.name: Sargasso of the Sisters
bodies.summary: A disk of dead magic around the Sisters, 700 miles across and 5 miles thick. No magic works in it, so a ship's helm stops.
facts: A disk 700 miles across and 5 miles thick
No magic works. The helm stops after 1 round, and a helmsman who stays falls unconscious in the second round.
The helmsman stays in a coma for 1d4 days after the ship leaves
A ship moves in a straight line at tactical speed, which is 400 miles a day for each point of Ship Rating

bodies.name: The Great Sargasso
bodies.summary: A sphere of dead magic about 1 million miles wide, in the dark between the Spectre and the shell. It cannot be seen. It follows a path of nested circles.
facts: Between the Spectre and the shell. The last of its circles is 6,000 million miles from Oerth.
Four nested circular paths, each with its own radius, tilt and speed
Only a sargasso detector can find it

bodies.name: The Habitat
bodies.summary: A dark blue-grey ellipsoid about 1 mile long and half a mile wide. Yellow light streams from its circular windows, and strange creatures look out of them. Nobody knows who built it.
facts: About 1 mile long and half a mile wide
Circular, 7,000 million miles from Oerth, at right angles to the ecliptic. One orbit takes about 800 months.
Thousands of cones 10 yards wide and high, with windows 5 yards across between them
No ship can come nearer than 100 yards. A ship that tries moves outward again at the same speed.
Scrying fails. The caster saves or falls into a coma for 1d6 hours.

bodies.name: Dark Stars
bodies.summary: Three or more black spheres, each some miles wide, in the gulf between the Spectre and the shell. They are totally black and give no light. Tales say that one touch destroys an object.
facts: Spheres some miles across. Their gravity reaches about 500 yards from the surface.
They give no light. They can be seen only when they go in front of a body that gives light.
No ship has landed on one and survived
Between the Spectre and the shell. The book gives no orbit.

spheres.name: Krynnspace
spheres.summary: The crystal sphere of Krynn's solar system. The Sun stands at the center, and six planets and an asteroid cluster orbit it. The gods shape this sphere more than its residents do.
facts: It looks like a sparkling disk. It is millions of miles deep. Nothing breaks it.
6 planets and 1 asteroid cluster, the Stellar Islands
16: 1 at Reorx, 3 at Krynn and 12 at Zivilyn
Circular portals open at random. Each has a silver-blue edge and is 1 yard to almost half a mile wide. Only things with some life can go through.
Wizards connect the openings to the orbits of Krynn and Sirion. When the two planets are near each other, the openings become larger and more numerous.
The stars are small portals to the quasi-elemental plane of Radiance. A new star appears for each good soul who dies for others.
The lakshu are a fey race of about 60 warriors who sail in a number of ships. The reigar, a legendary race, study the stars, the clouds and the moons of Krynn.

bodies.name: The Sun
bodies.summary: The primary of Krynnspace, fixed at the center of the sphere. White-hot flames leap from its surface. Helians and efreet live on it, and no ship came closer than one million miles and lived.
facts: None. It stays at the center.
Creatures from the elemental plane of Fire. Helians live in towers, and more than 50 efreet roam.
Crews are at risk from 20 million miles out. Ships burn at one million miles.

bodies.name: Sirion
bodies.summary: The planet nearest to the Sun. Basalt islands float on a boiling sea of magma, and steam hides the two poles. Efreet and azar operate the only ship dock, on the north pole.
facts: Creatures from the elemental plane of Fire, and plasmen
One, on the north pole between the efreet and azar communities. The descent through the steam takes 15 turns.

bodies.name: Reorx
bodies.summary: The second planet from the Sun, a world of sheer mountains and deep chasms. Dwarves and gnomes mine it, and mindflayers keep slaves in tunnels far below. It has four docks for ships and one moon.
facts: 4. The largest sit on flat mesa tops. Ships of mindflayers and neogi stop elsewhere.

bodies.name: Ora of The Hammer
bodies.summary: The only moon of Reorx. Explorers know only a small part of it. It has the conditions for life. About 20 dwarf miners came here recently and hide in a cave from monsters.
facts: Circles Reorx. The book gives no distance or period.
Monsters of wildspace: salt wiggles, swamp wiggles, q'nidar, argos and delnoric plasmoids
About 20 dwarf miners from Reorx, who wait for rescue in a cave

bodies.name: Krynn
bodies.summary: The third planet from the Sun. Its population is larger than that of all other bodies in the sphere together. The gods monitor it most.
facts: Mostly humans. Also elves, dwarves, kender, merfolk and others.
2. One is next to Palanthus on Ansalon, and one is in the Imperial City on Taladas. Only about one person in twenty knows about spelljamming.

bodies.name: Solinari
bodies.summary: A moon of Krynn that clouds always hide. From Krynn it looks like a ball of mist. One side always faces Krynn, and the far side is bare rock.
facts: Faces Krynn. It has trees, lakes and low hills.
Circles Krynn at the same distance as the other two moons (the distance is an estimate). One orbit takes 36 days.

bodies.name: Lunitari
bodies.summary: The largest moon of Krynn. It has many pools of water, tall shrubs and grasses, and a cloudless sky. Hidden residents make a wrecked ship look haunted, so visitors do not stay.
facts: Pools of water, tall shrubs and grasses. The sky has no clouds.
Four watcher beholder-kin, a pair of old hadozee, five neutral DeGleash plasmoids and one rastipede
Once every 10 years it eclipses the Sun for a number of hours.
Circles Krynn at the same distance as the other two moons (the distance is an estimate). One orbit takes 28 days.

bodies.name: Nuitari
bodies.summary: The smallest moon of Krynn. It looks black from far away because of its dark mountain spires and near-black mosses. Evil creatures live here and kill the crews of ships that stop here.
facts: Black mountain spires, a small number of trees and many deep green mosses
Evil creatures: argos (the number is unknown), DelNoric plasmoids, a handful of lutums and a small number of lensman beholder-kin
Ships that stop here are taken, and their crews die.
Circles Krynn at the same distance as the other two moons (the distance is an estimate). One orbit takes 8 days.

bodies.name: Chislev
bodies.summary: The fourth planet from the Sun, a jungle from pole to pole with no oceans. Giants and dragons rule it, and humans and demihumans are rare. Shou Lung explorers class it as a liveworld.
facts: Spherical earth body. Shou Lung explorers class it as a liveworld.
Humans and demihumans. Giants and dragons are the dominant species.
None. One cleared field of about 3 square miles, near the equator, serves merchants.

bodies.name: Zivilyn
bodies.summary: The largest planet in the sphere, an air body made of the pieces of a shattered world. Boulders as large as continents and as small as a fist turn in its air. Twelve moons orbit it in a ring.
facts: 12 moons, each named for a god
Stranded humans and demihumans. Colonies live on the moons.
Land Wrecker, a boulder as large as Ansalon, and the Triad, three boulders at the core

bodies.name: Paladine
bodies.summary: A moon of Zivilyn with craters and deep chasms, as if a disaster struck all of it. Small plants live in places, and tiny streams flow. No animals live here.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Craters and chasms across the globe
Small plants and streams, but no animals
Explorers look for the cause of the disaster, and miners look for minerals.

bodies.name: Majere
bodies.summary: A moon of Zivilyn covered with mountains, caves and tunnels. The weather is chilly, and snow stays on the tallest peaks. Dwarves from Reorx mine copper and silver here.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Mountains with caves and tunnels, and little flat land
One, a flat site a mile square between two mountains. Visitors get free lodging.
Copper and silver for ale, cloth, leather and food

bodies.name: Kiri-Jolith
bodies.summary: A temperate moon of plains where herd animals roam. The wizard Gray Mark claims it and lives in a castle that he shaped from the ground. His guardians chase visitors away.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Temperate plains with herds of animals
The wizard Gray Mark, who keeps settlers out
Grommams, giant space hamsters, wyverns, q'nidars, golems, salt wiggles, chimeras and gnolls

bodies.name: Mishakal
bodies.summary: A bare rock, like Chemosh. Signs of earlier life stay, such as human bones and cooking tools. A company of humans digs there for an ancient city.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Bare rock with signs of old life
A company of humans digs for what they think is an ancient city.

bodies.name: Gilean
bodies.summary: The largest moon of Zivilyn. Clouds of dark orange and rose hide it, and a lush tropical world is below them. Elves and half-elves live here.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Warm tropical land under clouds of dark orange and rose
Fruit, vegetables and liquor for cloth, household goods and books

bodies.name: Shinare
bodies.summary: A large, warm moon like Gilean, but with almost no clouds. A small number of elves live here in seclusion and hide from visitors.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Warmer than Gilean, with less wind
A small number of elves, who live apart

bodies.name: Takhisis
bodies.summary: A temperate moon of grassland, small forests, springs and mountain ranges. Primitive humans live here and hide from visitors. The moon has the name of a god of evil.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Grassland, small forests, streams and mountain ranges
Primitive humans who hunt herd animals. A small number of tribes farm.

bodies.name: Sargonnas
bodies.summary: A desert moon of cactus, dry plants and rocky sand. A handful of blue dragons use illusions to lure ships down and then attack the crews.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Desert with white clouds and little rain
A handful of blue dragons, with insects, snakes and rodents
Illusions of oases, crashed ships and farms draw ships to the dragons.

bodies.name: Morgion
bodies.summary: The smallest moon of Zivilyn, a swamp world with shallow water and moss-draped trees. Black dragons, wyverns and lizardmen live here.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Water from 20 feet deep to only inches deep, with huge moss-draped trees
Medicinal plants, which sell for high prices on Toril

bodies.name: Chemosh
bodies.summary: A bare rock with no water, plants or animals. Skeletons and tools show that humans lived here long ago. Some explorers think it was part of Zivilyn before the world broke.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Bare rock, with old arrowheads, pottery and human bones
Some explorers think the gods threw it into orbit when Zivilyn broke.

bodies.name: Zeboim
bodies.summary: The only ice-covered moon of Zivilyn. It has frozen lakes, snowy mountains and permafrost, though it shares the orbit of the warm moons. White dragons, yeti and remorhaz live here.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Frozen lakes, snow-covered mountains and permafrost
Remorhaz, yeti, ice toads, winter wolves and white dragons
The moon is cold, but it follows the same orbit as the warm moons.

bodies.name: Hiddukel
bodies.summary: A temperate farm moon with flat, fertile plains and frequent rain. Settlers of many races farm giant vegetables and sell them to merchants. It has three docks for ships.
facts: Circles Zivilyn in a ring with the other 11 moons, at an equal distance. The book gives no distance or period.
Flat, fertile plains with frequent rain
Human, gnome and elf farmers with a democratic government
Giant vegetables for household goods, clothes and fine items

bodies.name: Nehzmyth
bodies.summary: An egg-shaped world with a dark swamp from pole to pole. Its other name is the Vanishing Planet, because it passes through the Black Clouds and seems to vanish for months. Neogi and umber hulks hold caves below the swamp.
facts: Neogi and umber hulks. Aquatic umber hulks live in the lakes, and swamp treants walk the surface.
None. The neogi capture any ship that stops there.

bodies.name: Stellar Islands
bodies.summary: An asteroid cluster, the seventh world from the Sun. Five oasis asteroids hold the settlements, and each is 100 to 400 miles wide. Enchanted ribbon walkways connect them, and good residents who stay three months receive maximum hit points.
facts: Giff, dracons, gnomes, grommams and spacesea giants
Five oasis asteroids. The largest has an active volcano, and the other four have tall waterfalls. Smaller rocks up to 1 mile across have no residents.
None. Ships can use the pools below the waterfalls.

bodies.name: The Black Clouds
bodies.summary: A choppy ring of black clouds on the same orbit as Nehzmyth. They are invisible against the sky, and they scald each person who touches them. They hide Nehzmyth when it goes through them.
facts: A ring on the orbit of Nehzmyth, 900 million miles from the Sun
Invisible against the sky. Starlight shows through, but Nehzmyth does not.
A touch scalds for 2d4 damage each turn. The heat does not damage objects.
Evil and neutral characters who die in the clouds vanish. Good characters stay as bodies.
A crew that goes through forgets the clouds.
Souls of evil humans and demihumans who die in wildspace collect in the clouds. The clouds become larger as more die.

bodies.name: Clouds of Freezing Vapor
bodies.summary: Thin, almost clear clouds of ice crystals, 1 to 100 miles thick. They orbit Krynn most frequently and also occur around Nehzmyth and the Stellar Islands. The gods use them to hide their acts.
facts: Most often in orbit around Krynn, and around far bodies such as Nehzmyth and the Stellar Islands
Nearly clear. The ice crystals flicker white, pale yellow and blue.
The gods use them to hide their acts. Scrying with a crystal ball or a wizard eye spell fails against them.
A ship goes through safely. Each crew member must make a saving throw against spells, or stare at the crystals for 1d4 turns.
5d10 cold damage each round. A character at minus 10 hit points shatters, and no wish can revive the character.

spheres.name: Herospace
spheres.summary: Herospace has nine small suns, and each sun has one planet. Each planet is the home of one of the nine types of hero, from lawful good to chaotic evil. The Magistrates control the sphere from the moon Borden and let only proven heroes live there.
facts: 9, one for each of the nine alignments
Borden, the only moon, circles Ge'Neva
The Rational Order of Magistrates, 20 members, on Borden
The Order meets each ship that enters with 10 hammerships
A shard in the color of a sun is the pass to its planet
The book gives no distances. The map shows estimates.

bodies.name: Light blue sun
bodies.summary: A small light blue sun with one planet, Ge'Neva. The map puts it in the middle of Herospace. The book names no middle sun, but the Magistrates live on Ge'Neva's moon.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
At the center. The book names no center, so this is a choice.

bodies.name: White sun
bodies.summary: A small white sun with one planet, Gondorin. Only a white crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Gondorin, home of lawful good heroes

bodies.name: Light orange sun
bodies.summary: A small light orange sun with one planet, Cumberland. Only a light orange crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Cumberland, home of neutral good heroes

bodies.name: Light purple sun
bodies.summary: A small light purple sun with one planet, Woodhaven. Only a light purple crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Woodhaven, home of chaotic good heroes

bodies.name: Gray sun
bodies.summary: A small gray sun with one planet, Asylum. Only a gray crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Asylum, home of chaotic neutral heroes

bodies.name: Dark green sun
bodies.summary: A small dark green sun with one planet, Chaostromme. Only a dark green crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Chaostromme, home of chaotic evil heroes

bodies.name: Dark blue sun
bodies.summary: A small dark blue sun with one planet, Morgan's World. Only a dark blue crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Morgan's World, home of neutral evil heroes

bodies.name: Blood red sun
bodies.summary: A small blood-red sun with one planet, Darkseed. Only a blood-red crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Darkseed, home of lawful evil heroes

bodies.name: Yellow sun
bodies.summary: A small yellow sun with one planet, Hearthguard. Only a yellow crystal shard gives entry to that planet.
facts: Small sun, much smaller than a usual sun
Hearthguard, home of lawful neutral heroes

bodies.name: Ge'Neva
bodies.summary: The home of neutral heroes. Forest covers most of it, and it has more wildlife than the other planets. Many druids live here, and Borden, the home of the Magistrates, circles it.
facts: Forest covers most of the surface
Borden, the only moon in Herospace
Many druids. Other settlers live alone in manors.
Tests for settlers are harder here than on the other planets

bodies.name: Gondorin
bodies.summary: The home of lawful good heroes. Its geography is orderly and symmetrical, and its seasons have equal length and are easy to predict. Summers are warm in all places, and winters are cold.
facts: Seasons of equal length, easy to predict. Warm summers and cold winters in all places.
A base with at least 30 hammerships
A base with at least 30 hammerships

bodies.name: Cumberland
bodies.summary: The home of neutral good heroes. It looks most like the lands of Krynnspace, Greyspace and Realmspace. It is warm at the equator and colder near the poles, and taverns and merchant houses are plentiful.
facts: Arctic mountains, temperate hills and dry deserts
The most social planet. It has taverns and merchant houses, but no cities.
The sage Keriacus lives here, near the Off-World Inn.

bodies.name: Woodhaven
bodies.summary: The home of chaotic good heroes, and the most beautiful planet in Herospace. It has grassy hills and large forests, and the weather is fair. The light purple sun rises at the same time in all places.
facts: Rolling grassy hills and large forests
Fair, with little change between the hemispheres
Mostly elves, a close and family-like people

bodies.name: Asylum
bodies.summary: The home of chaotic neutral heroes. Ruins of ancient buildings fill all of its surface, with sewers below the streets. A settler's home repairs itself and fills with riches in one night, but the riches become worthless off the planet.
facts: Gray sun (the text calls it dull gray)
Ruined city streets over the whole surface, with sewers below
Mindless humans, called grunts, who serve the settlers as slaves
Homes repair themselves and fill with wealth. The wealth rots away off the planet.

bodies.name: Chaostromme
bodies.summary: The home of chaotic evil heroes. It looks beautiful in the light of its emerald sun. Wildlife and plants are plentiful, and the climate becomes colder near the poles. Orcs, giants and other violent humanoids live in the wilds.
facts: Dark green sun (the text calls it emerald)
Mixed, and colder near the poles
Orcs, giants and other violent humanoids
Heroes who fight in the wilds win, but gain no experience levels

bodies.name: Morgan's World
bodies.summary: The home of neutral evil heroes. It is dark and misshapen, with twisted trees, mountains shaped like grim faces, and harsh rain. When the dark blue sun is down, the air causes trances in which the mind sees its wishes as fact.
facts: Twisted trees and rocks, and mountains shaped like grim faces
Causes trances while the sun is down. The mind sees what it wishes.
From Morgan Darkdawn of Greyspace, the first settler

bodies.name: Darkseed
bodies.summary: The home of lawful evil heroes. Its blood-red sun gives weak light, and the sky is dark for many days at a time. The plains are flat and have no landmarks, so travelers cannot find their position.
facts: Flat, endless plains with no landmarks
A cool, steady wind blows all the time
Often total darkness for many days
The Magistrates answer many calls from lost travelers

bodies.name: Hearthguard
bodies.summary: The home of lawful neutral heroes, and the planet with the smallest population. It is hot, rocky and barren, and desert covers most of its surface. The Magistrates have no record of trouble there.
facts: Hot and harsh. Desert covers most of the surface.

bodies.name: Borden
bodies.summary: The only moon in Herospace, a barren world with no life. The Magistrates live here, in buildings named for their purpose. Their fleet here has 60 hammerships.
facts: The Rational Order of Magistrates, who rule Herospace
60 hammerships, twice the 30 or more at each planet base
No living person holds a pass to Borden

spheres.name: Greatspace
spheres.summary: Greatspace has a yellow sun, Lanth, with seven planets and an asteroid belt. Its Citizens trust science more than magic and honor the Greek gods. The Shambrath family of Thesalys rules the sphere.
facts: An asteroid belt between Longpoint and Hecht
A vampire's artifact hides the light of Lanth
The book gives no distances. The map shows estimates.

bodies.name: Lanth
bodies.summary: The yellow sun in the middle of Greatspace. In the story, an artifact of the vampire T'Laan hides its light with a spell of continual darkness. The fires of the sun continue to burn.
facts: 1 asteroid belt, between Longpoint and Hecht
T'Laan's artifact hides its light. The sun seeds of Faeriespace lift the darkness at once.

bodies.name: Karrington
bodies.summary: The planet nearest to Lanth, a hot and lifeless world with no water and a thin atmosphere. The ground reaches 600 degrees at the closest point of its orbit. No one lives there.
facts: Up to 600 degrees at the closest point of its orbit
None. No water and no features on the surface.

bodies.name: Skora
bodies.summary: The second planet. Violent storms fill its poisonous methane atmosphere. Nobody lives there, but a rumor says that the wizard Klemen prepared a home on it with magic.
facts: None. A rumor tells of the wizard Klemen's home.

bodies.name: Thesalys
bodies.summary: The third planet and the home of the Shambrath family, the rulers of Greatspace. It has many climates and cultures, and five governments share it. The Shambrath family leads the strongest one.
facts: Five major governments. House Shambrath is the strongest and rules all of Greatspace.
Castle Skyview, home of House Shambrath
Scientific. The Citizens honor Zeus and the other Greek gods.

bodies.name: Myle
bodies.summary: The only moon of Thesalys. Bruin Shambrath built a hidden shelter on it, where he goes to be alone. Nobody else knows of it.
facts: Built by Bruin Shambrath. Even his father did not know of it.
A good base for the heroes

bodies.name: Lagor's World
bodies.summary: The fourth planet. The astronomer Lagor found it about 850 years ago. Its climate is like that of Thesalys, but somewhat colder. About 50 human cultures live there, with some gnomes and halflings.
facts: About 850 years ago, by the astronomer Lagor
Much larger than that of Thesalys. About 50 human cultures, with gnomes and halflings.
Weak, because of the many cultures and the weaker economies

bodies.name: Longpoint
bodies.summary: The fifth planet, a giant world that Lagor found almost nine centuries ago. It was the farthest known planet at first, and so it has its name. Violent earthquakes and volcanoes shake it, and nobody lives there.
facts: Nearly nine centuries ago, by the astronomer Lagor

bodies.name: Asteroid belt
bodies.summary: A belt of asteroids around Lanth, between Longpoint and Hecht. It covers about 85 percent of its orbit, so a ship that goes to the outer planets almost always finds it. Small pirate bands live in it.
facts: Small bands, many at war with local officials
A pirate community of about 150 fighters and over 300 others, with 10 converted ocean ships
Raids make travel to the outer planets hazardous

bodies.name: Hecht
bodies.summary: The sixth planet, a wild and mountainous world with the smallest population in Greatspace. Humans and elves live there in small, isolated communities, and they honor rangers and druids. Its inhabitants know almost nothing about the trouble on Thesalys.
facts: Humans and elves. The smallest population in Greatspace.
A peaceful haven where the heroes can regroup

bodies.name: Boran
bodies.summary: The seventh planet and the farthest from Lanth. It is a frozen, almost lifeless world, and large arctic storms hit its surface. White dragons, yeti and arctic trolls live there.
facts: Almost none, apart from white dragons, yeti and arctic trolls

spheres.name: Darkspace
spheres.summary: Darkspace is a dead sphere with no living sun. A vast, dark husk of a sun sits in the middle, and rocks as large as moons and small planets orbit it. The vampire T'Laan rules the undead that roam there.
facts: The husk of a dead sun
Rocks in many orbits, some as large as moons and small planets
Always cold, with strong, biting winds
Once a sphere of nine planets. Only the third, Verin, held advanced life.
The book gives no distances. The map shows estimates.

bodies.name: The Dark Sun
bodies.summary: The dead sun in the middle of Darkspace. Only a vast, dark husk remains. It gives no light or heat. The sun seeds of Faeriespace can make it burn again.
facts: Husk of a dead sun (once a fire body)
Debris in many orbits, and the rock Verin
Sun seeds relight it with an 80% chance
The sphere is always cold, with strong, biting winds

bodies.name: Debris field
bodies.summary: Rocks of unknown and strange nature that orbit the dark sun at many distances. Some are as large as moons and small planets. Undead made by T'Laan roam on them.
facts: Some as large as moons and small planets
Many different orbits around the dark sun
The book calls it debris of unknown and strange nature

bodies.name: Verin
bodies.summary: The largest rock in Darkspace, almost as large as a planet, in the orbit farthest from the dark sun. It was the third of nine planets and had a living human culture. Its life is gone, and T'Laan's Tower of Night stands on it.
facts: Rock nearly the size of a planet
The farthest from the dark sun
Once the third of nine planets. Its human people died in the Time of Death.
The vampire T'Laan, from the Tower of Night
Spectres, wraiths, shadows, ghouls, zombies and skeletons
New Thesalys, a camp of stranded Citizens of Greatspace, 20 miles from the tower
Dark, dead plains with no life

spheres.name: Faeriespace
spheres.summary: Faeriespace has no central sun, because one enormous tree fills the sphere. Sixteen suns hang from its branches like fruit, and eight planets sit on the branches. The inhabitants live in peace as one community, and Aelivere, the One-King, is their ruler.
facts: The Great Tree, an enormous living tree
16, hung on the branches as fruit
8 on the branches: 4 low (Vastdarken) and 4 high (Upgood)
Armon, where the trunk splits in three
Shifting leaves hide the suns from the planets in turn
The book gives no distances. The map shows estimates.

bodies.name: The Great Tree
bodies.summary: An enormous tree that fills the sphere. No sun stands in the middle of it. Its roots end at the bottom of the shell, and its branches and leaves have their own gravity and hold air. The leaves move to make night and day.
facts: Living tree, the primary of the sphere
End at the bottom of the shell
The branches and leaves have their own
Armon, where the trunk splits in three
Isopterites, giant termites, tunnel in the trunk

bodies.name: Armon
bodies.summary: The capital of Faeriespace, at the point where the trunk of the tree splits in three. It is the only community that is not on a planet. About 30,000 creatures of many races live there in peace, and Aelivere lives in a palace of giant mushrooms.
facts: Ggaarin elves, Raczmar gnomes, Dulan dwarves, Mratzal drow, Wellow goblins, humans and dragons
Never dark. Once a month (Month's End) the suns are all hidden and the Great Crystal of the Moon glows.
Giant mushrooms outside, with endless rooms inside

bodies.name: Tree sun 1
bodies.summary: One of the sixteen burning suns that hang from the tree like fruit. The leaves of the tree move and hide it from the planets at times.
facts: Burning sun, a fruit of the Great Tree
1 of 16, twice the number of planets
Shifting leaves hide it and so make night on the planets

bodies.name: Morath
bodies.summary: One of the four lower planets of Faeriespace, called Vastdarken. It rests on the lower branches of the tree. The sky is always overcast and stormy, and evil creatures live here.
facts: Planet resting on a branch of the Great Tree
Peaks, deserts, moors, hills and forests
Evil races such as behir, chimeras, trolls, goblins and harpies
Not truly evil, because Faeriespace sees good and evil as one whole

bodies.name: Genla
bodies.summary: One of the four higher planets of Faeriespace, called Upgood. It rests on the higher branches of the tree. Good creatures such as elves, nymphs and unicorns live here.

spheres.name: Clusterspace
spheres.summary: An ancient sphere with two suns and no planet-sized rock worlds. Thousands of asteroids, planetoids and gas giants fill it, and many hold settlements. Any ship can enter, but only a living ship can leave.
facts: Firefall, a size I cluster of fire bodies
Denaeb, a sapphire sun on a steeply inclined orbit
Five: Calimar, Deyomad, Mordan, Trinona and Ushathrandra
The book gives 8,000 million miles from the Fringe to the inner track of the map
Ships pass in with no trouble. Only living ships can leave. A spell cannot open a portal to the Flow from inside.
13 towers topped by flame move along the inside of the shell. They mark the months and the years.
Antilans, illithids, Varan, Calidians, neogi, Thoric, dwarves, elves, lizard men and beholders

bodies.name: Firefall
bodies.summary: The primary of Clusterspace, at the center of the sphere. It is a cluster of fire bodies of many colors that circle each other. Spheres of flame rise and fall in a regular pattern.
facts: Cluster of fire bodies, size I
The sun-fountain. The Antilans call it Pyrax.
Denaeb and every other body in the sphere
The Sun Mages power their crystal ships and their sunmagic with its energy

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Islands of the Sun
bodies.summary: An asteroid belt between the two suns. It is too hot for most beings, so only fire elementals and similar creatures can live there. Rumors say that the Sun Mages built shielded fortresses here.
facts: Magically protected Sun Mage fortresses serve as a place to retreat in war

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Denaeb
bodies.summary: The second sun of the sphere. It is a sphere of sapphire flame on a steeply inclined orbit. Its light is dimmer than the light of Firefall. Some mages think that it is shrinking.
facts: Spelljammers see flickers in its center

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: The Shakalman Group
bodies.summary: A cluster of earth bodies that holds the largest shipyard in the sphere. The Antilans build crystal ships and crystal citadels here in secret. Human slaves supply the labor.
facts: Cluster of earth bodies, size C
A tiered pyramid 8,000 feet on each side. It is the only working builder of crystal ships and citadels.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Barukhaza
bodies.summary: A cluster of hollowed asteroids that was once the richest mine in the sphere. The ore is almost gone. The dwarves now make weapons and serve as Antilan shock troops.
facts: Weapons, armor, jewelry, gems and mercenaries

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Golden Girdle
bodies.summary: The richest asteroid belt in the sphere and the center of the Antilan Empire. Water, sunlight and good soil are plentiful. Three artificial worlds orbit in it.
facts: The Antilans keep it for their own ships and drive other ships out

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Kashimar
bodies.summary: An artificial world shaped like a hemisphere, 300 miles across. Its flat side faces Firefall. It holds the Crystal University, where the Sun Mages store their magical lore.
facts: The greatest Sun Mages and their slaves
The store of Antilan magical knowledge
It turns slowly, so it has a day and a night
Three worlds form a triangle around Firefall, all at the same distance
