The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Mu-Thalak
bodies.summary: An artificial hemisphere world, 300 miles across, and the capital of the Antilan Empire. The great noble houses, their slaves and the army live here. No other race has landed on it.
facts: Noble houses, their slaves and the Antilan military
Closed to every race but the Antilans
Homes of many-colored crystal and streets of copper

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Tan-Sharm
bodies.summary: An artificial hemisphere world, 300 miles across, closed to all but the Antilans. Some say the Antilan gods live there. Antilan ships attack any ship that comes within 100 miles.
facts: Closed to all but the Antilans and their slaves
Ships within 100 miles come under attack
Some say the Antilan gods live there

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Tumara Cloud
bodies.summary: An air nebula only 700 miles across. The Antilans built floating towns in it on crystal platforms. It is their naval base, where they build and repair crystal ships.
facts: More than 100 illithid attacks on it failed in one Cycle

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Malishan
bodies.summary: A large blob of water with a few small chunks of earth, all inside one shared atmosphere. It began as a comet, fell into a stable orbit and thawed. The Antilans use it as a watering post and a base for local invasions.
facts: Cluster of water and earth bodies, size C
A comet of ice and earth that fell into a stable orbit
A watering post and a staging base for local invasions

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Dumovian
bodies.summary: A cluster of earth bodies that was once a group of Calidian city-states. The Sun Mages now breed slaves here. Rumors of a slave revolt are constant.
facts: Cluster of earth bodies, size D
Once a group of Calidian city-states
A slave-breeding belt of the Sun Mages
Rumors of slave revolt never stop, but the Sun Mages still rule

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Mordan
bodies.summary: A size G gas giant with three major moons. The Sun Mages and the Calidians hold the moons.
facts: Spherical air body (gas giant), size G
The Sun Mages and the Calidians hold its moons

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Iatan
bodies.summary: A moon of Mordan that the Calidians hold. It is a farming colony that sends food to their distant settlements. The Antilans plan to take it in time.
facts: A farming colony for distant Calidian settlements

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Thuma
bodies.summary: A water moon of Mordan with a small population. The Sun Mages value it because its water supplies their inner settlements.
facts: A water world, so it supplies the inner Sun Mage settlements

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Sharya
bodies.summary: A moon of Mordan with many resort settlements. They serve the pleasures of every race.
facts: The Sun Mages and the Calidians hold the three moons of Mordan

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Shaseogan
bodies.summary: A small asteroid that the neogi pulled out of the Inner Ring into a new orbit a little inside it. Tethered platforms circle it. The neogi sell Inner Ring goods to Antilan captains here.
facts: The neogi moved it out of the Inner Ring ten Cycles ago

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Inner Ring
bodies.summary: The crowded asteroid belt at the heart of the Cluster. Millions of asteroids hold nearly every race, but not the beholders. Trade is fast, and the Neogi Agreement bans war here.
facts: The Neogi Agreement bans war and gives the neogi a share of all profit
Dark areas that large asteroids hide from the sun. Undead and hostile creatures live there.
A dense area of small ports, each less than 5 miles across

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Atalan
bodies.summary: A mass of water globules that circle a large city. It is the center of Antilan power in the Inner Ring. It began as a watering station for crystal ships.
facts: The best food in the Ring, and trade in magical goods
Strong. Most ships near it are crystal ships.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Sharona
bodies.summary: A forested sphere 900 miles across. It is the largest trading port in the Inner Ring and a refuge for Calidian noble houses. Most of it is closed to other races.
facts: Most of it is closed to people who are not Calidians

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Thundazar
bodies.summary: A mined-out dwarven world where Antilans and Calidians work together. From orbit it looks dead, but a large city lies below the surface. The Calidians make jewelry from nearby gold and gems.
facts: The only place where Antilans and Calidians work together

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Illiman
bodies.summary: A mass of water globules around a few lumps of earth. The neogi bought it from the lizard men several Cycles ago. It is the new neogi homeworld.
facts: Visitors need a valid reason, and trade is not one

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Chakarak
bodies.summary: A new dwarven colony on an asteroid about 21 miles across. It looks like a clump of earth with trees. The dwarves design new weapons for spelljamming ships, and other dwarves call them rebels.
facts: Its designs are in use on neogi decks and illithid ships

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Varan Group
bodies.summary: One of the largest groups of land masses in the Cluster, ruled by Varan warlords. The illithids built fortresses and outposts here with Varan consent. The center is cold and dark.
facts: Cluster of earth bodies, size D
Varan warlords, with illithid fortresses and outposts
Cold, close to freezing at the center, which large asteroids shade

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Ushathrandra
bodies.summary: A purple gas giant. The illithids stopped it in its orbit with magic, and its three moons stand frozen in its shadow. The moons are the seat of the illithid empire.
facts: Spherical air body (gas giant), size F
More than 3,000,000, mostly illithids and Varan
Ruined human cities lie inside the gas

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Illimandra
bodies.summary: The nearest moon of Ushathrandra, 15,000 miles across and covered with pale-blue ice. It is the true seat of illithid power. More than 2,000,000 illithids live here.
facts: Nearest moon, on the dark side of Ushathrandra
Slave cities and dangerous magical research

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Talos
bodies.summary: The middle moon of Ushathrandra, 1,000 miles across, with a silvery-black surface and a core full of water. It supplies water to the other two moons. The illithids use it as a light prison colony.
facts: The smallest of the three moons
Second moon, on the dark side of Ushathrandra
The watering base for Illimandra and Darkwatch

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Darkwatch
bodies.summary: The outermost moon of Ushathrandra, 1,000 miles across, with a silvery-black surface. The illithids call it the moon of death. Their mage caste lives here.
facts: Magical center of the illithid empire and its first line of defense

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Deyomad
bodies.summary: A huge purplish-green gas giant with a dense ring system. It is the homeworld of the beholder races. The beholders destroy any ship that enters its space.
facts: Spherical air body (gas giant), size F
A dense ring system with asteroids of up to size C
The beholders attack every ship that enters

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Rings of Deyomad
bodies.summary: A dense ring system around Deyomad. Asteroids of up to size C are common in it, and the beholders use most of them. Spies report huge asteroids covered with slaves.
facts: Asteroids of up to size C
The beholders work most of the asteroids

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Phalangilon
bodies.summary: A living asteroid about 1 mile across, covered with spines and bits of wreckage. About 100 psionicists live in it as one fused mind. It can read any mind in the Cluster.
facts: The oldest living asteroid in the Cluster
A strong psionic presence that psionic characters feel from up to 50 miles away

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Glacier
bodies.summary: An asteroid belt of cold earth and frozen ice, mostly ice. The Calidians run a few trade cities here and export water. Beholders and illithids are strong here, and they fight often.
facts: Calidian cities export water to dry colonies
One outpost that supplies water to the dry colonies near Firefall

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: The Dark Group
bodies.summary: Five asteroid clusters that remain from a world the First Cataclysm destroyed. Ruins from before that time cover them, and undead fill the ruins. The illithids and the Varan hold most of them.
facts: Cluster of earth bodies, size C
Achemon (Calidian), Torin (Varan), Khel (illithid), Lumura (illithid) and Mitiar (Calidian)

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Calimar
bodies.summary: A massive gas giant of black and red with ash-gray storm clouds. Its three moons hold mines. The illithids and the Varan took the mines from the Calidian settlers.
facts: Spherical air body (gas giant), size G
2,400,000, Calidians under illithid and Varan rule
Metal ores, gems, water and shadowstone

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Amaron
bodies.summary: The largest moon of Calimar, 10,000 miles across. It holds gold ore and red diamonds. The illithids conquered it, but a few Calidian groups still hide in sealed tunnels.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Calamed
bodies.summary: A moon of Calimar, 1,000 miles across. It has underground springs and a lichen that is good to eat. The Calidians settled it second.
facts: Some ore, many underground springs and an edible lichen

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Sultamar
bodies.summary: A moon of Calimar, 1,000 miles across, with a molten core of lava. The Calidians settled it first. They left when flames and magma burst into their mines.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Thandilan
bodies.summary: A small sphere of earth where the Calidians run a rich farming kingdom. The farmers ship crops to less fertile settlements. Dwarf mercenaries and Calidian lanceships guard it.
facts: The most valued farmworld in the Cluster, so it is well guarded
Dwarf mercenaries and lanceships that orbit it

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Boyarny
bodies.summary: A green cluster of earth bodies with fields, orchards and small forests. Varan and Thoric settlers share it, and no illithids rule it. The Varan trade fruit and vegetables.
facts: Cluster of earth bodies, size C
Fresh and dried fruit and vegetables, and breeding stock
None on the surface. Ice crystals in orbit supply it.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Avarien
bodies.summary: A tangled cluster of infinity vines and clods of earth with an elven city inside. The elves trade only on their own terms and let no ship land. The vines attack any non-elven ship that touches them.
facts: Live cluster of infinity vines, size C
Food, Megalier wine, star charts and transport out of the sphere

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Tronsogard
bodies.summary: A cluster of earth bodies and a remote Thoric settlement of explorers and traders. It is rough, and its equipment is simple to repair. Spelljammer captains like that equipment.
facts: Cluster of earth bodies, size B

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Drachengard
bodies.summary: A cluster of ice and earth asteroids, and the best starting place for adventurers. Its orbit rises above and sinks below the ecliptic, so its ice freezes and thaws.
facts: Cluster of water bodies, size C
About 200 years ago, by a Thoric who killed a radiant dragon
It bobs high and low through the ecliptic on its track

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Sargasso of Skulls
bodies.summary: A zone where magic does not work. A ring of strange skulls marks its edge, and a purple cloud hides the inside. Old spacers tell wild tales about what lives there.
facts: A ring of strange skulls shows the edge
A purple cloud blocks the view

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Cerekazadh
bodies.summary: The largest dwarven nation in the Cluster, on an asteroid 110 miles across. One side is carved into a dwarven face, and its mouth is the landing port. The dwarves sell weapons, tools and armor.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Trinona
bodies.summary: A small gas giant with two thin ring systems and a large moon, Netune. The Calidians formed the Grand Duchy of Trinona here. Platform villages float inside the gas.
facts: Spherical air body (gas giant), size F
Mining towns in the rings and platform villages in the gas
The platform villages sell strange magical goods

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: First Ring System of Trinona
bodies.summary: The inner of two thin ring systems around Trinona. Calidian mining towns and villages stand in the rings.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Netune
bodies.summary: The large moon of Trinona. It lies between the two ring systems. Some believe that its haunted ruins are the source of the strange goods that the platform villages sell.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Second Ring System of Trinona
bodies.summary: The outer of two thin ring systems around Trinona. Calidian mining towns and villages stand in the rings.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Ssthakal
bodies.summary: A cluster of water worlds and a home of the Astromundi lizard men. They deal with outsiders more freely than the lizard men of Khalzan. They are known as fighters and scouts.
facts: Cluster of water bodies, size B
Fighting skill, and work as scouts and explorers

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Giltiond
bodies.summary: One huge vine grown around many earth asteroids and large balls of ice. A scattered tribe of elves lives on it and eats its fruit. They have become savage and xenophobic.
facts: Liveworld of one huge vine, size B
Fruit, vegetables and water pods from the vine
The elves guard the vine, and they are dangerous

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Ironport
bodies.summary: A pyramid of iron that the neogi had the dwarves build around an asteroid. It is a trade port and a place of entertainment. Battles are banned within 100 miles of it.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Maw
bodies.summary: A fully grown murderoid, a savage living creature of size B. The books class it as a liveworld. Local people avoid it, and outsiders who try to land on it suffer for it.
facts: Adult murderoid, a liveworld, size B
Outsiders who try to land on it come to harm

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: The Great Belt
bodies.summary: An asteroid belt of earth, water and ice. It is smaller and thinner than the Fringe, but more people live in it. Large parts of it are empty.
facts: Asteroid belt of earth, water and ice
The Thoric came first, then the Calidians, elves, dwarves and neogi
Many small communities depend on each other. Large parts are empty.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Dalmania
bodies.summary: A Calidian city that covers a pale clod of earth 25 miles across. It is the strongest of the outer powers. It needs nearby farm asteroids for food and water.
facts: Clothes, wood and goods from outside the Cluster

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Doromakhad
bodies.summary: A dwarven mining colony. Strange amoeboid creatures attacked it and have not been seen since. The dwarves have added heavy ballistae and other defenses.
facts: Heavy ballistae and other new defenses

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Hatha
bodies.summary: A frozen asteroid 80 miles across, with a blue-white surface and a biting wind. Thoric settlers hunt fur animals here. They also sell strange artifacts from deep below the surface.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Highport
bodies.summary: The remains of a dwarven citadel with a new iron tower on top. It is the only spaceport that the Arcane hold in the Cluster. A purple beacon on the tower shines for thousands of miles.
facts: A tower 1,400 feet tall, 3 miles around at the base
Calidians for ship repair and neogi for trade. The Arcane rule it.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Isle of Banshees
bodies.summary: A cold, dark asteroid 3 miles across. Undead sailors who died in the Cluster live here and attack ships that come near. Four shattered metal towers stand on it.
facts: Varies. Zombies, skeletons and other undead.
Shadowstone and items from before the First Cataclysm

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Khalzan
bodies.summary: A wobbly sphere of water with chunks of silvery-black stone in it. It is the largest lizard man settlement in Clusterspace. Only the neogi trade with the lizard men here.
facts: The lizard men do not let other races land
Ruined cities float inside the water

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Fringe
bodies.summary: The outermost asteroid belt. It is sparse, and most asteroids are too small to hold air. The Thoric hold the few that have air, and they supply ice to the rest of the Cluster.
facts: The book gives 8,000 million miles from the Fringe to the inner track of the map
The Thoric hold the colonies on asteroids that have air

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: The Shtokan Nebula
bodies.summary: A starfish-shaped cloud of water vapor and poison gas that floats near the inside of the shell. It orbits at right angles to the plane of the other bodies. A crossing is often deadly.
facts: Irregular nebula of poison gas, size D
The gas quickly kills those who are not ready for it
It is an evil sign when it lines up with a constellation on the first day of a month

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide

bodies.name: Constellation of Pyrax
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Pyrax. Chief god of the Antilans. The Antilans also use his name for Firefall.
facts: Pyrax. Chief god of the Antilans. The Antilans also use his name for Firefall.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Munigur
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Munigur. A god of the Calidians who wants peace kept.
facts: Munigur. A god of the Calidians who wants peace kept.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Gelanicus
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Gelanicus. An Antilan goddess of death, honored by Antilan women.
facts: Gelanicus. An Antilan goddess of death, honored by Antilan women.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Seltaine
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Seltaine. A god of evil that the Varan once worshiped. Worshipers are leaving him.
facts: Seltaine. A god of evil that the Varan once worshiped. Worshipers are leaving him.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Hordent
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Hordent. The god of the Thoric.
facts: Hordent. The god of the Thoric.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Tradifos
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Tradifos. A Calidian god of wildspace who protects travelers.
facts: Tradifos. A Calidian god of wildspace who protects travelers.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Yul
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Yul. A Thoric god of death and wealth.
facts: Yul. A Thoric god of death and wealth.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Fiira
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Fiira. A new sun god that Antilan slaves honor.
facts: Fiira. A new sun god that Antilan slaves honor.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Chodak
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Chodak. The dwarven god of battle and mining.
facts: Chodak. The dwarven god of battle and mining.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Regis
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Regis. The male half of the elven god. He is the god of battle.
facts: Regis. The male half of the elven god. He is the god of battle.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Wajek
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Wajek. The female half of the elven god. She is the goddess of hunting.
facts: Wajek. The female half of the elven god. She is the goddess of hunting.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Sstasa
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Sstasa. The god of the lizard men, who call him the god of everything.
facts: Sstasa. The god of the lizard men, who call him the god of everything.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

bodies.name: Constellation of Lugribossk
bodies.summary: One of 13 constellations, a tower topped by pillars of magical flame. It honors Lugribossk. The dread god of the illithids. His constellation dates from soon after the Second Cataclysm.
facts: Lugribossk. The dread god of the illithids. His constellation dates from soon after the Second Cataclysm.

sources.title: The Astromundi Cluster: The Astrogator's Guide
The Astromundi Cluster: The Celestial Almanac

spheres.name: Refuge
spheres.summary: A small sphere near Realmspace that the Arcane control. One large sun has a planet named Below, its moon Refuge, and a small outer planetoid named Welcome. Ships in trouble come here for repairs, supplies, and aid.
facts: Part of the Arcane Inner Flow. Realmspace is 7 days away.
30 days. The trip back takes 45 days.
The planet Below, the moon Refuge, the Salvage Ring, and the outer planetoid Welcome

bodies.name: The Sun
bodies.summary: The large sun at the center of Refuge. One planet and one small outer planetoid orbit it, and a moon orbits the planet.
facts: Large. The article gives no size letter.
The moon Refuge, the Salvage Ring, and the outer planetoid Welcome

bodies.name: Below
bodies.summary: An uninhabited world of dense tropical jungle and shallow seas. Passing ships can take free fresh water and air here. The Arcane stock the planet with monsters to keep visitors away.
facts: Planet with dense tropical jungle and shallow seas
None. The Arcane bring in monsters from hundreds of worlds.
Ships can take free fresh water and air.
The moon Refuge and the Salvage Ring
A hidden base. The Arcane sell paid monster hunts on the planet.
The Arcane tell visitors not to land. Assassins and pirates also use the hunts to kill targets.

bodies.name: The Salvage Ring
bodies.summary: A huge ring of old ship hulks and scrap that are tied together. It orbits Below, inside the orbit of Refuge. The Arcane sell its parts to damaged ships.
facts: Ring of scrap and ship parts
Around Below, inside the orbit of Refuge
The Arcane buy old hulks and ask no questions
Hired Giff patrols stop thieves and settlers
Pirates, scavvers, and other monsters hide in it

bodies.name: Refuge
bodies.summary: The only moon of Below and the largest off-world ship base that humans know. The Arcane build and repair ships here. The surface looks like one large garden, and secret tunnels run under it.
facts: Moon with a garden surface and tunnels below
2 docks, each for 30 ships. Two emergency bays stay open.
A ring of 24 space golems, plus catapult and ballista turrets
Hidden crowns of the void and many plants renew the air
Banks, the Great Vault, hotels, hospitals, a casino, and taverns
The Arcane act as judges. Most punishments are fines and loss of goods.

bodies.name: Welcome
bodies.summary: A small planetoid at the outer edge of the system. It holds a naval base of at least 50 ships that escort or tow damaged ships to Refuge.
facts: At least 50 ships of all designs, with humans and halflings loyal to the Arcane as crews
Escort or tow damaged ships, hold plague ships and bomb ships, and stop running battles
Hidden repair docks in caverns and covered craters
Glowmoss Gardens on the surface give it its own glow
About a dozen sarphardin stay near it

spheres.name: Pirtelspace
spheres.summary: A cold, thinly settled sphere named for the explorer Anthonius Pirtel, the Ice Mage. A cool red star has a frozen world, a water world, a narrow asteroid belt, and an asteroid shell. A magic-dead region, the Sea of Sorrow, is in the shell.
facts: 2 worlds, 1 asteroid belt, and 1 asteroid shell
About 2,000 million miles (20 days of travel from the star)
Bitter cold. About 30 degrees F at Century's orbit. It is warmer nearer the star.
Black and white swirls with many portals. Alastriel is the one portal that these articles name.
30 days of travel through the Flow. The journey in the opposite direction takes 45 days.
38 days of travel through the Flow. The journey in the opposite direction takes 45 days.

bodies.name: Pirtel
bodies.summary: The cool red star that is the primary of Pirtelspace. Its light is weak. The Arcane named the star and the sphere for the explorer who found them.
facts: Weak and ruddy. The Mor Wake adds a red tint.
Anthonius Pirtel, the Ice Mage, who vanished while he explored the star
A water world, a frozen world, an asteroid belt, and an asteroid shell

bodies.name: The Mor Wake
bodies.summary: A thick shell of asteroids around the star. The rocks are as large as small moons, and they hit each other. The shell gives the star's light a red tint.
facts: Some are as large as small moons. Most have no air, but a small number hold plants and thin air.
Night scavvers, a gravislayer, and a neogi stronghold
The Sea of Sorrow moves in the shell

bodies.name: The Sea of Sorrow
bodies.summary: An invisible magic-dead region in the Mor Wake. Spells, magic items, and helms do not operate in it. Its position changes at random, so no chart can mark it.
facts: Magic works only in a 50-mile radius around the Lich's Tear
About 24 derelict ships, night scavvers, and the lair of the dragon Blacklight
A battle between the Ice Mage and two liches made the Lich's Tear, which causes the sargasso

bodies.name: The Lich's Tear
bodies.summary: A black sphere, hundreds of yards across, in the heart of the Sea of Sorrow. It causes the sargasso. An object that touches it is destroyed or sent away.
facts: Black sphere with a hostile light
The Ice Mage's sphere of annihilation met a gate that the lich Delgranoth opened
An object that touches it has a 60% chance to vanish and a 40% chance to go to a different plane or sphere
The hulk of a space leviathan orbits it. The radiant dragon Blacklight lairs in the hulk.
A creature that stays less than 100 miles from it for a week can turn violent and chaotic evil

bodies.name: Archin
bodies.summary: The one world of Pirtelspace that persons can live on. A deep azure ocean makes up most of its surface, with many small islands. Humans, halflings, and sea elves live here.
facts: Humans and halflings on the islands, and sea elves called illanti in the ocean
Hasturia in the west. Noccolante and the Quarinaron Confederacy in the east.
The Ice Mage taught the Quarinaron merchants spelljamming. They sail flying galleons.

bodies.name: Skyport
bodies.summary: A gray stone disk, 500 yards across, that orbits Archin at a height of hundreds of miles. It holds a small walled town and a 300-foot tower. The Ice Mage built it as his stronghold.
facts: 500 yards across, with a tower 300 feet high at the hub
Hundreds of miles above Archin, at right angles to the surface
17 stone wharves, and one wharf serves as a dry dock
Grandmaster Azure, a wizard, and Admiral Gerard Antarra
Pirtel built it about 500 years ago. Quarinaron merchants took control of it after he vanished.

bodies.name: Guinmir's Band
bodies.summary: A sparse belt of rocks, 10 to 500 feet across. Some sages say it is what remains of a planet named Guinmir. Ships can fly above or below it with no trouble.
facts: Some sages say a planet named Guinmir orbited here long ago
Dwarves mined asteroids here long ago. A small number of emptied citadels are in the belt.
The drow castle Oloth Kulggen stands on one asteroid

bodies.name: Oloth Kulggen
bodies.summary: A ruined castle on an asteroid in Guinmir's Band. The drow mage Tanthalyn repaired it with walls of stone and named it. A small drow garrison holds it.
facts: Oloth Kulggen means "Shield of Darkness" in deep drow
A ruin that Tanthalyn found and repaired
About 20 drow and a drow damselfly ship
3 catapults and 3 ballistae on the roof
A stone dock with room for an elven man-o-war

bodies.name: Century
bodies.summary: A frozen ball of ice and rock that takes 100 years to orbit the star. One side always faces the star, and the other side is always dark. Human barbarians live on the sunward side.
facts: Frozen world of ice and rock
Equal to its year. One face always points at the star.
Human barbarian clans on the sunward side, and frost drow on the dark side
War between the barbarians and the frost drow in the Lands of Gray Ice

bodies.name: Darkwatch
bodies.summary: A ruined elven military outpost on a small asteroid that orbits Century above the dark side. The elves built it to hold the stranded drow on the planet. The radiant dragon Blacklight destroyed its patrol and supply ships.
facts: Ruined outpost on a small asteroid
The elven Imperial Fleet, to keep the drow on Century
200 warriors with their families, and two men-o-war
The elves have been dead for more than 200 years
Skeletons of more than 300 elves, and the annals of the outpost
The sword Winnower, a radiant dragonslayer, lies in the ruins

bodies.name: Alastriel
bodies.summary: A bright star on the crystal shell. It is a permanent portal into the Flow. Persons on Archin see it as a star.
facts: Portal on the crystal shell, seen as a bright star
On the shell, 14 days of travel from Oloth Kulggen
Near it, drow open a gate to Realmspace. The gate ends 100 miles from Realmspace's shell.
The gate grows for 5 days, then collapses in one week

spheres.name: Darnannonspace
spheres.summary: A sphere in the Arcane Inner Flow that elves control. Pirtelspace lies between it and Refuge. Rumor says it holds a major port of the elven Imperial Fleet.
facts: Elves. The Flow diagram calls it the Elven Sphere.
More than 2 months of travel, through Pirtelspace
38 days of travel. The trip back takes 45 days.
Rumor says it is a major port of the elven Imperial Fleet
The Arcane trade here. An Arcane envoy was lost on the way to talk about a new trade agreement.
Smiths here forged the sword Winnower for the Darkwatch commander

spheres.name: Vodonispace
spheres.summary: The home sphere of the Vodoni Empire. Its sun went nova 400 years ago, and a shell of asteroids called the Web surrounds the three inner planets. Emperor Vulkaran rules twelve spheres from the Imperial City on the planet Vulkarus.
facts: Vodon Prime, a small star that is not stable. It went nova 400 years ago.
Four: Sala, Vulkarus, Grog and Calandia
A shell of asteroids around the three inner planets. It is the wreck of the fourth planet, Kathyk.
Black crystal. Gems set deep in it look like stars.
Magic that uses other dimensions does not work. This includes teleport, dimension door and all summoning spells.
No priest can pray for a spell above level 2. The gods of the sphere are locked in the Eye of the Gods.
The vortex on Sala doubles the damage of fire magic. A fireball can do up to 20d6.
Years are Anno Vulkarus (AV), or Promo Nova before the nova. The adventure year is 463 AV.
The Vodoni name large moons by number only, such as Calandia One and Grog Two.

bodies.name: Vodon Prime
bodies.summary: The only star of Vodonispace. It is small, and it gives off a flickering blue-gray light. It went nova 400 years ago and is not stable.
facts: Star, the primary of the sphere
A flickering blue-gray light. From the shell it looks like a small blue-white beacon.
About 400 years ago. The Vodoni fled before the blast and came back after it.
Its energy is not stable. It blocks magic that uses other dimensions.
Believers in the banned gods use it as their beacon.
Four planets and the Web orbit it.

bodies.name: Sala
bodies.summary: The innermost planet, a large ball of molten lava. The nova made a vortex to the Elemental Plane of Fire in it. Fire magic does double damage in the sphere.
facts: Molten planet, a ball of lava
The first planet, nearest to Vodon Prime
A vortex to the Elemental Plane of Fire. Elemental creatures can go in and out through it.
The vortex doubles the damage of fire magic. A fireball can do up to 20d6.
The vortex closes when the Elemental Lord of Fire is freed. Sala then becomes a usual molten world.

bodies.name: Vulkarus
bodies.summary: The second planet and the capital of the Vodoni Empire. It is a large, green jungle world with three oceans and six continents. The Imperial City, the only city in view from space, has the crystal Imperial Palace.
facts: Jungle planet, the second from Vodon Prime
Vodon, in Appendix A and on the book's system map
Three oceans and six continents. Plants fill the continents, but not the polar caps.
A city miles across, built like a spider web. The crystal Imperial Palace at its center touches the edge of space.
Vulkaran filled the planet with animals and plants from conquered worlds. It was the only body full of life after the nova.
Below it are the ruins of the former capital, Hithandia. They form the Undercity, where enforcers are made.
Thousands of ships sail near the planet, and the Imperial City has docks.

bodies.name: Grog
bodies.summary: The third planet, a farm world with a smooth surface of volcanic ash. The surface has seas of amber grain and large freshwater pools. Slaves do the farm work, and the planet has two moons.
facts: Farm planet, the third from Vodon Prime
The ground is smooth, with a layer of volcanic ash miles deep. The soil is one of the richest in the galaxy.
Freshwater pools and seas of amber grain. There are no salt oceans.
The seasons are never harsh. Crops can be harvested all year.
Two moons, Grog One and Grog Two. The two moons are uninhabitable.
Slaves receive plots of ground and can marry and have families. They have more freedom here than anywhere else in the empire.
No military bases and no militia. Some enforcers and breeders are on duty there.
The planet works like one large feudal estate, with castle-like keeps at important sites.

bodies.name: Grog One
bodies.summary: One of the two moons of Grog. The Vodoni name large moons by number, so Grog One follows their rule. Nobody can live on it.
facts: The book prints Grog Two as an example of a Vodoni number name. Grog One follows from it.

bodies.name: Grog Two
bodies.summary: One of the two moons of Grog. The book prints this name as an example of a Vodoni number name. Nobody can live on it.
facts: A Vodoni number name. The book gives it as an example.

bodies.name: The Web
bodies.summary: A large shell of asteroids around the three inner planets. It is what remains of Kathyk, the fourth planet, which the nova destroyed. The rocks have so much energy that ships cannot go through it safely.
facts: Asteroid shell around the inner system
The nova broke up Kathyk, the former Vodoni home world. Kathyk was named for the first Vodoni emperor.
Between Grog and Calandia. It surrounds Sala, Vulkarus and Grog.
A ship needs 2 to 5 days to go through it. Vodoni breeders steer through with eagle vision. Other ships almost always take damage.
No safe path exists. This is why most Vodoni forces stay in the other spheres.
Buildings, mines and parts of cities of the former Vodoni culture are in the rocks.
Drawn as a wide ring. The book describes a shell.

bodies.name: Calandia
bodies.summary: The outermost planet, a small ball of ice with a blue tint. It is cold and barren, with icy mountains. Slaves mine gems here for the Vodoni.
facts: Frozen planet, mostly a ball of ice
The fourth and outermost planet, beyond the Web
Kathyk shielded it from the blast. The planet received some heat and a rain of debris.
Dozens of former mine complexes. One mine is active, on an icebound plateau.
The active mine has more than 2,400 slaves and almost 250 enforcers, with six werewolf ships on the plateau.
Two blind white dragons, Lukio and Babia, live by the mine. They attack the enemies of the Vodoni. Their lair holds a large hoard of rough gems.

bodies.name: Calandia One
bodies.summary: The only moon of Calandia, a cold world. The Vodoni hold slaves in a mining colony on it. Bright orange domes mark the colony from space.
facts: Moon of Calandia, a cold world with a Vodoni colony
A Vodoni number name for a large moon
One large dome, four small domes and a square storehouse, all painted bright orange
First stop for new slaves. It is a mining outpost and a supply stop for Vodoni patrols.
About 200 slaves row the galleys and learn to mine.
Galleys rowed by slaves, and a warship, dock at the colony. The galleys also train the slaves in space.

spheres.name: Golotspace
spheres.summary: Dragons and other magical beasts rule the skies of this sphere. Its humans, the Golotians, live in a mystical and superstitious culture like that of Greyspace long ago. Vulkaran keeps an uneasy truce with the dragons, who rule as regional barons.
facts: The book describes one planet. It names no star, planet or moon.
The Golotians are humans. Their culture is mystical and superstitious, like that of Greyspace thousands of years ago.
Dragons and similar magical beasts rule the skies. They control daily affairs like regional barons.
Vulkaran beat the red wyrm, the dragons' champion, in single combat. The dragons agree that no single dragon can beat him.
Vulkaran stays overlord. The dragons cannot unite under one leader, and the humans suffer.

spheres.name: Gorthspace
spheres.summary: A sphere at the center of the Vodoni Empire. Its one habitable planet, Gorth, has lush, ancient forests. Only animals live there, and Vodoni enforcers go there to hunt.
facts: At the center of the Vodoni Empire. This makes it a good place for enforcers to hunt when they are off duty.
Gorth is the only habitable planet. The book names no other body.
Animals only. The book knows of no sentient life.

bodies.name: Gorth
bodies.summary: The only habitable planet of Gorthspace. Lush, ancient forests fill it. It has animals but no known sentient life, and Vodoni enforcers hunt there.
facts: Forest planet, the only habitable planet of the sphere
Animals only. The book knows of no sentient life.
A favorite hunting ground for Vodoni enforcers when they are off duty

spheres.name: Kofuspace
spheres.summary: A solid sphere. Black shell material fills it to the core, and its worlds are air bubbles in the rock. Each of the three large bubbles has a small sun at its center, and the peaceful Kofu have farms in them.
facts: Solid black crystal shell material from the shell to the core
Large air bubbles in the solid material. The book calls them planets and names none.
Each of the three large bubbles has a small star at its center.
Portal tunnels join the bubbles. They open at random, but it is possible that strong beings can control them. A ship must find a tunnel by chance and sail down it quickly.
The Kofu look like drow elves but have none of the drow powers or weaknesses. They are farmers with large farms, and they do not know what night is.
The Vodoni keep only a small number of garrisons in each bubble.

spheres.name: Kra'akenspace
spheres.summary: A sphere with no large gravitational bodies. Large green floating asteroids of porous organic material fill it, and breathable air fills all of the sphere. The winged Kra'aken live in large floating biospheres.
facts: No planets or other large gravitational bodies
Breathable air fills all of the sphere. Travelers often mistake it for a node of elemental air.
Large, green, floating masses of porous organic material, like plant life
The Kra'aken are slender, semi-transparent, winged humanoids. They are kind and telepathic, and they live in large floating biospheres.
The Kra'aken often shorten their name to Kra', so that nobody mistakes them for the giant squid-like monster of a similar name.
The Kra'aken have no spelljamming technology and are not fond of magic. They make friends, ask for a ride or pay for passage.

bodies.name: Green floating asteroids
bodies.summary: Large green asteroids of porous organic material, like plant life, float all through Kra'akenspace. The sphere has no planets, and breathable air fills it.
facts: The Kra'aken live in large floating biospheres

spheres.name: Lostspace
spheres.summary: A burned-out husk of a sphere. War, not a natural disaster, caused the ruin. Weapons and the remains of ships and cities are everywhere, and nobody knows what happened to the former inhabitants.
facts: Burned out. The book says no natural catastrophe caused the damage.
Arcane weapons of war and the remains of ships and cities are everywhere.
Nobody knows what happened to the former inhabitants. Vulkaran wants to find out.
Vodoni breeder research teams search all of the sphere for knowledge and advanced weapons.
Unusual artifacts, new spells and new spelljamming technology

bodies.name: Wreckage of the war
bodies.summary: The remains of ships and cities, and arcane weapons of war, fill this burned-out sphere. Nobody knows what happened to the people who lived here.

spheres.name: Passarspace
spheres.summary: A sphere with no native life and no central star. Asteroids and planetoids fill it. The Vodoni prize its natural resources and keep mining colonies and battle stations here.
facts: None. The sphere has no central star to give light or heat.
Asteroids and planetoids. Whether any of them are planets depends on how large a planet must be.
Vast natural resources, which Vulkaran prizes

bodies.name: Asteroids and planetoids
bodies.summary: Asteroids and planetoids fill Passarspace. It has no central star and no native life. The Vodoni mine them and keep battle stations among them.

spheres.name: Salzarspace
spheres.summary: One small water planet is at the center, and eight fiery stars roll along the inner face of the shell. When two stars touch, they go through each other in a fiery explosion. The Salzarians are living balls of water, each about 500 feet across.
facts: One small water planet at the center of the system
Eight fiery stars roll along the inner face of the shell. Two stars that touch go through each other with a fiery explosion.
Magic does not operate here, not even spelljamming devices. Ships move by oar, sail or physical flight only.
Portals in the shell open and close at odd times.
The known Salzarians number only in the hundreds. Each is a ball of water about 500 feet across, immune to all magic and almost immortal.
One of the first spheres that Vulkaran attacked. Only one Salzarian died, and the Salzarians agreed to follow his decrees. No Vodoni outposts are here.

bodies.name: The water planet
bodies.summary: A small world of water at the center of Salzarspace. The book gives it no name. Eight fiery stars roll around it on the inside of the shell.
facts: Small. The book gives no size letter.
The Salzarians, living balls of water about 500 feet across

bodies.name: Fiery star I
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star II
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star III
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star IV
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star V
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star VI
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star VII
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

bodies.name: Fiery star VIII
bodies.summary: One of the eight fiery stars of Salzarspace. They roll along the inner face of the shell, and two stars that touch pass through each other in a fiery explosion.
facts: On the inner face of the shell

spheres.name: Thasiaspace
spheres.summary: A sphere with one large star, Lifegiver, and one large jungle planet, Thasia. The Thasians, intelligent plant beings, resisted the Vodoni invasion far better than Vulkaran expected. The Vodoni have only hundreds of satellite stations above Thasia.
facts: Lifegiver, one large star of an ordinary kind
Plant beings like shambling mounds, but with human intelligence
Vodoni enforcer diseases and attacks do not harm Thasians. They regenerate quickly and hide well.
Hundreds of satellite stations hover above Thasia. A citadel on the ground survives only for days before the jungle takes it.
In hundreds of years the Thasians can have space travel with their organic technology. Then the Vodoni hold will be tested.

bodies.name: Lifegiver
bodies.summary: The only star of Thasiaspace. It is one large star of an ordinary kind. The Thasians know it as Lifegiver.
facts: Large, ordinary star, the primary of the sphere
Lifegiver is the Thasian name for it.

bodies.name: Thasia
bodies.summary: A gargantuan jungle planet, the only planet of Thasiaspace. Dense plant life fills the land and the surface of the oceans. Ships that go down to its surface can vanish.
facts: Jungle planet, the only planet of the sphere
Gargantuan. The book describes a mini-sphere of concentrated life-force.
Dense jungle fills the land. The oceans are thick with plants at the surface.
Travelers who go down onto what looks like solid ground can find their ship gone when they come back.
Hundreds of Vodoni satellite stations hover above it. Citadels on the ground vanish in days.

spheres.name: Vergonspace
spheres.summary: A sphere of six inhabited planets that have fought each other for centuries. Vulkaran gives intelligence and weapons to all sides, to keep them weak. The human Vergon can retake the sphere if they unite.
facts: Six inhabitable planets. The book names none of them.
The planets have fought each other for centuries.
Vulkaran gives intelligence and weapons to all sides, so no Vergon warlord can become overlord.
Humans. They are powerful and warlike.
If the heroes defeat Vulkaran, the wars end in less than 100 years. Then a race more powerful and deadly than the Vodoni will threaten Free Space.

spheres.name: Vodonikaspace
spheres.summary: The sphere nearest to Vodonispace, where the Vodoni exodus ended. Five habitable planets orbit here, and the former race was erased. The largest group of Vodoni enforcers is here, and most Vodoni weapons are made on Vodonika.
facts: Five, all habitable. Each is as diverse and populated as Oerth or Krynn.
The Vodoni exodus ended here. The former race was erased.
The largest group of Vodoni enforcers is here. Most weapons for Vodoni ships and enforcers are made on Vodonika.

bodies.name: Vodonika
bodies.summary: The one named planet of Vodonikaspace. Its name means New Vodoni. Most weapons for Vodoni ships and enforcers are made here.
facts: Planet, one of five in the sphere
Most weapons for Vodoni ships and enforcers are made and forged here.
Populated and diverse, like Oerth or Krynn

spheres.name: Zalanispace
spheres.summary: The home of the Zalani, black gargoyle-like beings who look fearsome but prefer art and trade to war. Vulkaran made a truce with them, then conquered their empire in days. The Zalani make the ships of the Vodoni fleet.
facts: Black, gargoyle-like humanoids with gaping mouths and large black wings. They find these features lovely.
Peaceful. They travel as ambassadors and traders and prefer to negotiate.
Vulkaran conquered the Zalani empire in days.
The book speaks of Zalani home worlds in the plural. It names none of them.
The Zalani make all Vodoni ships. Each ship has the winged look of Zalani craft.
The Zalani have the most freedom of any race in the empire, because they are necessary to Vulkaran's plans.
A ghost ship that was a Zalani ambassador's vessel sails the phlogiston to find help for the Zalani.

spheres.name: Glowrings Sphere
spheres.summary: A crystal sphere that The Maelstrom's Eye shows only in the memories of the scro general Vorr. Years before the story, Vorr joined a boarding attack on a pyramid ship in this sphere. The text names no sun, world or moon here.
facts: The memories of the scro general Vorr, in chapters 2, 4 and 16
A boarding attack on a pyramid ship. Its lich commander killed 72 boarders. Vorr killed the lich.
The lich put one helm at the apex and one in a small building at the center.
None named. The text gives no sun, world or moon.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Maelstrom's Eye

spheres.name: Heartspace
spheres.summary: A crystal sphere named for its bloated red sun, the Heart, which swells and shrinks in a cycle of some hours and seems to beat. The planet Crescent holds a large library of knowledge. Teldin Moore visits it in The Broken Sphere.
facts: Crescent, Starfall and Loom are named. Loom is the most distant.
16 permanent portals. Ships slow to tactical speed at a portal. At full speed, a ship can go out of control.
From the Flow, the shell looks like an endless wall of mother-of-pearl.
A large library in Compact, the city on Crescent where ships from other worlds must land
Starfall has a large harbor. Its tavern, The Philosophers' Rest, draws sages and philosophers.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

bodies.name: The Heart
bodies.summary: The primary of Heartspace, a cool, dim, brick-red sun at the center of the sphere. It is more than ten times as large as the sun of Krynnspace. It swells and shrinks in a cycle of some hours, so it seems to beat.
facts: More than ten times as large as the sun of Krynnspace
Dim and cool. A person can look straight at it.
It swells and shrinks by a small margin in a cycle of some hours.
It is near the end of its life. In millions of years it becomes a cinder.
Three named planets: Crescent, Starfall and Loom

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

bodies.name: Crescent
bodies.summary: A planet shaped like a globe with a large bite taken out. All its inhabitants live on the curved inner surface. A large library of knowledge is in the city of Compact.
facts: The two horns stay fixed in space, and the curved body turns around the line between them.
Rough mountains, craters and wide cracks. Fast clouds show winds that can kill ships.
Smooth, ancient hills and fields of green and brown
All inhabitants live on the inner surface
Compact. Ships from other worlds must land there first. Patrol ships examine them.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

bodies.name: Starfall
bodies.summary: The next world out from Crescent. It has a large harbor where ships can buy almost anything. A tavern there draws sages and philosophers.
facts: The next world out from Crescent
A large harbor. Sellers on the docks offer almost anything.
The Philosophers' Rest, where sages and philosophers argue
Two hadozee sailors go ashore here and do not sail on with the Boundless

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

bodies.name: Loom
bodies.summary: The most distant planet of Heartspace. It is a large, yellow-white world shaped like an egg.
facts: The most distant planet from the Heart
Large. The text gives no number.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

spheres.name: Herdspace
spheres.summary: A crystal sphere with air and gravity on the inner side of its shell. Seas, mountains, forests and farmland fill the shell, and beasts as large as worlds walk on it. A bright yellow-white sun at the center fades to darkness at times and makes night.
facts: A yellow-white sun at the center. The gnome Dyffed says no world orbits it.
A deep layer of air lines the shell. The layer has a sharp top edge, hundreds of miles or more above the ground.
The sun fades to dim red and goes out, then lights again. The text gives no length.
A gate puts each entering ship in the air, away from the shell. The gates open at the same time each day, for about an hour.
Lakes in the shape of megafauna footprints. Their water stops magic items, such as helms. One lake is about 120 miles long.
Beasts as large as worlds walk on the shell. One stands about 1,200 miles high. The fal One Six Nine lives on top of its horn.
Rastipedes, insect beings with eight legs, live underground. They descend from the crew of a crashed spelljammer.

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Maelstrom's Eye

bodies.name: The Sun
bodies.summary: The primary of Herdspace, at the center of the sphere. It shines yellow-white and looks two times as large as other suns that Teldin knew. It fades to dim red and goes dark at times, which makes night.
facts: Sun at the center of the sphere
About two times as large as other suns Teldin knew
Bright yellow-white. Its disk looks smooth and plain.
It fades to red and goes out, then lights again. This makes day and night.
None. Dyffed says no world orbits it.
It hangs overhead at each point on the shell

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Maelstrom's Eye

spheres.name: Nexspace
spheres.summary: A small, dark crystal sphere with no stars. A ship needs about a day to sail across it. Nex, a rocky world with a mind of its own, sits at the center with two dozen tiny suns in orbit.
facts: Approximately 100 million miles. A ship needs about a day to sail across it.
Nex, a rocky world at the center
No stars. The only light comes from the mini-suns around Nex.
A cold cloud of small grains surrounds Nex, about an hour of travel out
A small, frozen air world, about six hours of travel from Nex
Only a small number of explorers returned. Fire bolts from the ground and chasing mini-suns attack ships near Nex.
Nex means 'violent death' in an ancient language

sources.title: The Cloakmaster Cycle: The Broken Sphere

Like that of Ansalon on Krynn

Sensed through the cloak and amulet. No one sees it up close.

About 2,000 leagues above Nex, in a band more than 100 leagues deep

One chases the Boundless and blisters the paint on its stern

Garrash, a fire world with a ring of fire
Living metal beings that fly in the ring. They cannot go out of the sphere.
It flew through the ring and left Vistaspace about 200 hours before Teldin came.

Prominences go up many thousands of leagues above the surface

About 45 days, by small fast currents

Three times the gravity of most worlds
Three large moons. They line up each 28 local days.

Elven ships patrol the world, and an alarm net surrounds it

A few stars and the red glow of the gas ring

Gas that glows a sullen red
Drawn far larger than its true size

Icarus had 15 made. Each one gives a ship energy from an artifact.

A planetary garrison holds the world

2 levels, a landing pit for a hammership, and a greenhouse dome for air
